hook: The stimulation ladder. Map your inputs before you remove them.
topic: The tiered input framework — mapping dopamine load by stimulus intensity
body:
**The stimulation ladder. Map your inputs before you remove them. Most people skip this step and fail.**

A reset without a stimulus inventory is guesswork. You don't know what's driving your threshold up, so you don't know what to reduce, in what order, or by how much. Removing everything at once is dramatic and unsustainable. Removing nothing while "being more mindful" does nothing.

The framework works in tiers. Tier one: low-intensity inputs — long-form reading, walking, conversation, single-focus work. Tier two: medium inputs — music, podcasts, email, structured video. Tier three: high-frequency, variable-reward inputs — social feeds, short-form video, notifications, news cycles.

The goal is not to eliminate tier three permanently. The goal is to drop to tier one and two long enough for recalibration to occur — typically 72 hours minimum for early signal, seven days for meaningful reset.

Once you've mapped your actual daily inputs against this framework, you know exactly what you're dealing with. You know which inputs are doing the most threshold work. You can make a specific decision, not a vague one.

Do the audit first. Then the protocol makes sense.

Audit tool is in the link in bio.
